I'm working through what maximal triangle-free means—a graph where adding any edge would create a triangle, but no triangle currently exists. This is equivalent to saying every non-edge connects two vertices that share a common neighbor. For n=13, I'm considering whether a cycle or something like a Kneser graph might be the classic example, since a simple 13-cycle is triangle-free but not maximal.

Actually, I realize a complete bipartite graph K_{6,7} works perfectly here. It's triangle-free by definition since bipartite graphs have no odd cycles, and it's maximal because any non-edge lies within one of the two parts—and both endpoints of such an edge are already connected to every vertex in the other part, so adding it creates a triangle. That gives me 42 edges total.
